posts.title: Visage Academy | Reactivating old course enquiries

copy.default:
The expensive mistake in training isn't always losing the lead.

Sometimes it's deciding that “not now” means “never”.

A course enquiry can go quiet because of timing, confidence, money or workload while the original intent is still there.

For Visage Academy, the 222Emails process went back to that unfinished intent instead of starting with another batch of new leads.

We identified relevant past enquiries, reopened the conversation with a clear reason to respond, and made the next step easy to understand.

That is the retention problem training businesses often miss: the buyer journey can pause without actually ending.

How is “not right now” handled in your academy today?

posts.title: Visage Academy | Reactivating old course enquiries

copy.default:
27 old course enquiries re-engaged. Eight places reserved. £8,940 in attributable potential booking value.

The interesting part was how many of these leads had never really rejected the offer.

They had simply never reached a decision.

Training businesses can easily treat ‘not now’ like ‘no’. When timing, confidence or cash changes, the original intent can still be there.

The 222Emails job was to find that unfinished intent and restart the conversation with a clear reason to respond.

For academy owners: what happens to someone who says, ‘I’m interested, just not yet’?
